hero.sub: Dead outlets, an old panel, wiring a previous owner left behind: some electricians won't come look at a mess. We will. We trace the cause, tell you what we found and give you your options and a price before any work starts. You're not left alone with it. Call (316) 213-4513.

sections.heading: Three Calls Made, and Nobody Will Come Look
body: The kitchen outlets have been dead since Tuesday. The breakers all look fine, the house is older, and somebody before you did some of the wiring themselves. You're in the driveway with your phone, three calls in.

One company took a message. One said they'd get back to you. One could come in a couple of weeks. You don't need a miracle. You need a person to come look and tell you the truth about what's behind the wall.

image.alt: Homeowner standing in a kitchen checking a dead wall outlet with a phone in hand

sections.heading: We Look First, Then Follow the Wire
body: Some electricians would rather skip a puzzle. We'd rather solve it. Older houses collect added circuits, spliced wires and breakers that were never the right size, and finding the cause means opening things up and following the wire.
Then we tell you what we found in plain words, with your options and the price, before any work starts. If a job is small, we say so.

sections.heading: Somebody Finally Came to Look
body: Being turned away is a lonely feeling. Something in your house doesn't work, and the people whose job it is have other things to do.
We don't want you to feel that. The first job is to show up, look at the mess and be straight with you about it. A tangle of old wiring is where we start, not a reason to say no.

sections.quote: First off Ben was willing to come take a look at our electrical mess when others wouldn't give us the time of day. Secondly his quote was fair and his guys were able to get on us on the schedule quickly.

sections.heading: Everything We Do
sections.intro: Repairs, lighting, panels and the bigger projects, for homes and for small commercial properties.

sections.heading: Electrical Repair in Wichita
body: A breaker that trips again right after you reset it is telling you something. So is an outlet that's warm, a discolored switch plate, a buzz or a burning smell. Loose connections heat up, so stop using that outlet and call us.
Outlets dead across half the house, a garage with no power or lights that flicker in several rooms each have a cause. We trace it.

sections.heading: Lights, Fans and Fixtures
body: A room with one dim fixture never feels finished. A ceiling fan where there's no wiring, lights for the back steps or a strip under the kitchen cabinets can change how a house feels to live in.
We wire new fixtures, put in recessed lights and hang fans, including fans in ceilings that never had a light, with the supports added.

sections.heading: Panel Upgrades
body: An old panel can be a safety problem. Fuse boxes, rust or scorch marks, double-tapped breakers and brands with a record of breakers that fail to trip, like Federal Pacific Stab-Lok and Zinsco, are all reasons to have it looked at.

So is a panel with no room left, or a small service in a house that now runs central air or an EV charger. An upgrade needs a permit and a city inspection, and the power company disconnects and reconnects service. Expect the power off for part of the day.

image.alt: Open electrical panel with labeled breakers in a garage

sections.quote: I really appreciate the excellent communication and how you took the time to explain the specific safety concerns regarding my Federal Pacific panel that other companies wouldn't address. It was incredibly helpful that you took photos and proactively checked in with the city inspector to ensure every detail of the project went smoothly.
sections.name: Wayne R.

sections.heading: New Outlets, New Circuits and Bigger Projects
body: Plenty of calls aren't repairs at all. You want an outlet where the coffee bar is going, power for a new stove or oven, a Level 2 charger in the garage.
We run the circuit and put in the outlet. We also handle sub-panels, rewiring, surge protection and generator hookups. When a job can go more than one way, we lay out the options and you choose.

image.alt: Level 2 electric vehicle charger mounted on a garage wall

sections.quote: Ben is very knowledgeable, honest, super creative does what's promised and reasonably priced! Ben has done multiple jobs for me over the years. After letting him know what I want, he always gives me a few options on how to move forward with my projects.

sections.heading: What Happens When You Call About a Repair
body: You tell us what's happening: which outlets, which rooms, what changed. We get you on the schedule, and we call before we arrive.
Then we trace it. We test, follow the circuit and find the failed part or the loose connection. You hear what we found in plain words, with your options and the price, before we fix anything.

image.alt: Electrician testing a wall outlet with a meter in a Wichita home

sections.heading: What the Signs Usually Mean
body: Here is what we see most, and what it tends to point to.

items.title: A breaker that trips again right after you reset it
items.text: An overloaded circuit, a short or a ground fault. A breaker that's warm or won't reset needs an electrician.

items.title: An outlet or switch plate that's warm or discolored
items.text: A loose connection, which heats up. Stop using it and call us.

items.title: Dead outlets in several rooms
items.text: Often one failed connection upstream, sometimes a breaker. We follow the circuit instead of replacing outlets one by one.

items.title: Lights that flicker in more than one room
items.text: One fixture is usually a bulb. Several rooms points to a loose connection or an overloaded service.

items.title: A garage or outbuilding with no power
items.text: A tripped ground-fault outlet, a bad breaker or a wire that has been cut or pulled loose.

items.title: A buzz, a crackle or a burning smell
items.text: Switch that circuit off and call us. Don't wait for the weekend.

sections.quote: Ben was very good at explaining every diagnostic step and found and corrected the problem, a bad breaker
sections.name: Mark N.

sections.heading: Older Houses and Other People's Wiring
body: Older houses pile up changes: added circuits, spliced wires, a breaker that was never the right size, work done by a previous owner. The wiring doesn't match any drawing.
That's work we take on. We open it up, follow the wire and tell you what's wrong and where it goes from there. If the fix is small, we say so.

sections.quote: Quick, efficient, and professional. Lost power to my garage and they fixed it up. Pointed out the previous home owners diy mess and pointed out where we go from there.
sections.name: Che J.

sections.heading: Repair, or Something Bigger?
body: Most repairs are small: a breaker, an outlet, a connection. Sometimes the cause is bigger, like an old panel that has no room left or a service that can't carry the house.
When that's the case, we say so and lay the repair next to the larger fix, with the cost of each. You decide.

sections.heading: Why We Don't Just Swap the Outlet
body: A new outlet on a bad circuit stops working again. So we test first, find where the power stops and fix that, not the symptom.
It takes a little longer than a swap, and you don't pay twice. If the answer is a cheap part, you hear that too. [[confirm: [X]-year warranty on our work]].

items.title: You hear the options and the price
items.text: We explain what we found and what it takes to fix it, before we start.

items.title: We fix it, check it and clean up
items.text: We confirm the circuit works and leave the place tidy.

sections.heading: Before You Call
body: Switch off the breaker for a circuit that smells hot or has scorch marks, and leave it off.
Note which outlets or rooms have no power and what happened right before. A new appliance, a storm or a recent project all help us find it faster.

items.q: Do you charge to come look at a repair?
items.a: We offer free estimates. We price the completed job, and you hear the number before we start.

items.q: Can you come the same day?
items.a: Often within a day or two. If something is wrong right now, say so when you call and we'll give you a time.

items.q: What if you can't find the cause right away?
items.a: We keep tracing it and tell you where we are. You don't pay for a guess.

items.q: Will you tell me if it's not worth fixing?
items.a: Yes. We tell you what we found, what it takes to fix it and whether it can wait.

body: A new light in a room that already has a fixture is a simple swap. A light or fan in a room with none, behind a finished ceiling, takes more work.
We look at the ceiling and the attic access first, and you get the price before the work starts.

sections.heading: Dimmers, Switches and Where They Go
body: A dimmer has to match the bulbs it runs, or the light buzzes and flickers. Tell us whether you use LED or older bulbs and we'll fit a dimmer that works with them.
A switch belongs where your hand goes when you walk in. If a room needs a second switch at the other door, or one moved, we can do that with the lights.

sections.heading: Outdoor and Porch Lighting
body: Outdoor fixtures need wiring made for the weather and a switch inside that you'll actually use. Back steps, a patio, the walk to the door and the corner of the garage are the usual spots.
We talk through what you want to see at night, then place the lights and run the wire.

sections.heading: Kitchens and Under-Cabinet Lights
body: Light on the counter makes a kitchen easier to work in. Under-cabinet lights can be hidden behind the cabinet edge, so you see the light and not the fixture.
We plan where the wire runs first, so the finished kitchen looks like nothing was done to it.

unverified.heading: What we couldn't verify, and why it matters
unverified.intro: We marked these on the demo as yellow "to confirm" tags instead of guessing, because we won't put a claim on your site we can't back up. Your current site says "years of experience" with no number, and shows no license number, warranty or list of towns.

items.why: A homeowner letting someone into an older house wants to know you've been doing this a while, and a made-up number is worse than none.
Someone with a panel or messy wiring wants to look up the license before they let you open the wall.
"Surrounding areas" doesn't tell a homeowner in a town outside Wichita whether you'll come look.
If a repair fails again, the homeowner who already made three calls wants to know you'll stand behind it.

unverified.closing: This is what our onboarding call nails down. Fifteen minutes, and every tag becomes a real, true line.

why: Your site says “With years of experience” and “integrity, expertise, and exceptional customer service,” and it shows the same four reviews on every page. Your reviews say something different: Ben came to look at an electrical mess when other electricians wouldn’t, and got the job on the schedule quickly. Today that sits on Google, not on your site.

The site also loses people before they read a word. On a phone it is laid out almost twice as wide as the screen, and the phone number isn’t a tap-to-call link. The Lighting card on your homepage goes back to the homepage.
So the demo tells one story: the electrician who comes to look at the hard ones. It opens with electrician in Wichita, KS, and gives electrical repair and lighting installation a page each.
